dossier.claim: Some Japanese expressions are read through their individual words or carried into English phrases that do not express their function in the scene. This can turn mental states into physical events or produce unusable collocations.
dossier.sourcePattern: 闇雲 describes aimlessness, 後ろ髪を引かれる describes reluctance to leave, 夢にも思えない intensifies impossibility, and 上の空 describes absentmindedness. Other examples concern leaving someone’s presence, treating someone with care, making a living, and introducing a practical fact.
dossier.englishEffect: The English supplies a cloudy night, tingling from behind, being inside a dream, and looking up at the sky. “Treat you importantly” and “use magecraft as a living” preserve nearby words without producing the intended English relation. Sakura’s departure becomes disappearing in front of Shirou, and a practical fact becomes “the actual problem.”
dossier.limits: Literal imagery and foreign proverbial allusions can work in English. They are not errors merely because an English proverb could replace them. These examples require a changed action, relation, or identifiable collocation fault; familiarity alone is not the standard. The successful evasive-speech and mental-collapse idioms limit the claim.
dossier.diagnostic: 35 findings in this category; 8 cited passages.
